extraction_text: 坚战请求毗湿摩讲述大神毗湿奴（伊沙/商部）的各种名号。
毗湿摩转述婆薮提婆之子（黑天）将讲述大神毗湿奴的名号。

relationships: 婆薮提婆之子（黑天）是主要讲述者

extraction_text: 婆薮提婆之子（黑天）入水沐浴，洁净自身后开始讲述大神毗湿奴的特征。
婆薮提婆之子（黑天）召集听众，包括坚战、众婆罗门首领和阿波迦的后代，准备讲述。

relationships: 婆薮提婆之子（黑天）是讲述者

extraction_text: 婆薮提婆之子（黑天）提到过去因商波（湿婆）的原因见到大神毗湿奴，并达到三昧境界。
瞻波瓦蒂在商波罗被始光杀死十二年后，请求婆薮提婆之子（黑天）赐予她一个儿子。
瞻波瓦蒂描述她想要的儿子：雄武有力、天下无敌、容貌伟岸、纯洁无瑕，像婆薮提婆之子（黑天）一样。

relationships: 瞻波瓦蒂向婆薮提婆之子（黑天）提出请求

extraction_text: 瞻波瓦蒂称赞婆薮提婆之子（黑天）的能力，认为三界之内没有他得不到的东西，甚至可以创造另一个世界。
瞻波瓦蒂提到婆薮提婆之子（黑天）曾十二年饮风为生，身体干枯，取悦于兽主（湿婆）。
艳光公主生了许多儿子，包括遮卢代始那、苏遮卢、遮卢韦沙、耶首陀罗、遮卢湿罗瓦兄弟、遮卢耶沙兄弟、波罗底优那和商部。

attributes.relationships: Mother-son relationships between 艳光公主 and her sons

extraction_text: The narrator (implied to be the husband/father) is asked by 艳光公主 to give her a son as powerful as the ones she already has.
The narrator agrees to fulfill 艳光公主's request but asks to leave for a period of time.
艳光公主 advises the narrator to go to 湿婆 (Shiva) and blesses him with protection from various divine and natural entities.

attributes.supernatural_elements: Invocation of Brahma, Shiva, Kashyapa, rivers, gods, seasons, etc., for protection

extraction_text: The narrator bids farewell to 艳光公主, then visits his father, mother, and King 阿护迦 to inform them of his journey.
The narrator visits 伽陀 and 罗摩 to seek their permission before departing.
The narrator summons 金翅鸟 (Garuda), who carries him to 大雪山 (the Himalayas).

attributes.supernatural_elements: Use of Garuda for transportation to the Himalayas

extraction_text: Upon reaching 大雪山, the narrator releases 金翅鸟 and observes the mystical environment, including the hermitage of 优波曼纽.

attributes.supernatural_elements: Description of divine hermitage, various trees, and natural wonders

extraction_text: The narrator describes a beautiful hermitage (净修处) with abundant natural resources and harmonious coexistence of animals.

attributes.details: The hermitage has fruit trees, ritual fire ashes, diverse animals living peacefully together (antelopes, elephants, tigers, lions, leopards, deer, peacocks, snakes, lynxes, buffaloes, monkeys), and pleasant sounds (streams, birds, elephants, celestial singers, chanting).

extraction_text: The narrator mentions the sacred and auspicious river flowing through the hermitage, identified as the daughter of Jahnu (阇诃奴的女儿).

attributes.details: The river is Ganga (Ganges), often called Jahnavi as the daughter of Sage Jahnu.

extraction_text: The narrator describes the ascetics (苦行者) living in the hermitage, each practicing severe austerities.

attributes.details: Ascetics practice various austerities: eating only air, water, smoke, fire, milk, foam, or light; living like cows or deer; using stones or teeth for food; constant meditation, chanting, or special baths.

extraction_text: The narrator states the hermitage is worshipped by gods, great beings, Shiva, and morally upright people.

attributes.details: The hermitage radiates light like the sun's disc and is revered by deities including Shiva.

extraction_text: The narrator observes harmonious interactions between natural enemies (snakes and mongooses, deer and tigers) due to the ascetics' spiritual power.

attributes.details: The ascetics' radiant energy (苦行者光芒闪耀) causes normally hostile animals to play together like friends.

extraction_text: The narrator enters the hermitage and sees an exceptional ascetic named Upamanyu (优波曼纽) surrounded by students.

attributes.details: Upamanyu is described as youthful, wearing tree-bark clothes, with matted hair, radiating light from austerities, and calmly seated with disciples. The narrator bows to him.

extraction_text: The speaker (Krishna) arrives and is welcomed by a sage.
The sage predicts that Krishna will have a son who resembles him.
The sage instructs Krishna to perform severe austerities to please the god Ishana (Shiva).

attributes.purpose: To gain Shiva's favor for progeny

extraction_text: The sage recounts that gods and sages previously attained their desires at this place by pleasing the supreme god through austerities.

Hiranyakashipu's son Mandara received a boon from Shiva enabling him to rival Indra for a million years.
Vishnu's discus and Indra's thunderbolt shattered when striking Mandara.
The gods defeated the asura chiefs who had received Shiva's favors.
Another asura, Vidhyutprabha, pleased Shiva and was made ruler of the three worlds for 100,000 years.
Shiva gave Vidhyutprabha ten million sons and the island of Kusha as his kingdom.
The asura Shatamukha performed a 100-year sacrifice using his own flesh, pleasing Shankara (Shiva) who granted him supernatural yoga power and undiminishing strength.
In ancient times, the self-existent Brahma performed yoga meditation for 300 years to obtain progeny, after which Shiva gave him a thousand immensely powerful sons.

attributes.action: Meditation for offspring and divine grant
attributes.relationship: Creator god receiving boon from Shiva

extraction_text: In ancient times, Mahabali (摩珂梵) slighted the dwarf sages (众矮仙人).
The angry Dwarf Sages performed austerities to please Rudra (Shiva).
Pleased Rudra granted them a boon to create a golden bird that would steal Indra's soma.
In the past, angry Rudra made all water disappear from the world.
The gods performed the Saptashata (七食钵) sacrifice to appease Rudra and obtained water from elsewhere for Earth.
Atri's wife, a Veda-knowing woman, abandoned her husband Atri, declaring she would no longer be under his control, and sought Rudra's protection.

attributes.relationships: Marital separation, wife seeks divine refuge

extraction_text: Fearing Atri, she fasted for 300 years and slept on wooden sticks for 300 years to please Bhava (Shiva).

Shankarya, an upright man, performed 900 years of mental worship to Bhava.
Pleased Bhava promised Shankarya he would become a writer with lasting fame across three worlds and a prosperous lineage.
Savarni, a famous sage from Satya Yuga, performed 6,000 years of austerities.
Rudra appeared, pleased, and promised Savarni he would become a world-renowned writer and achieve immortality.
The narrator (speaking to Krishna) claims to have personally seen Shiva through strict self-control.

attributes.relationships: Narrator addresses Krishna, describes personal experience

extraction_text: The narrator explains he obtained what he needed from Shiva.

The narrator and Dhumra played and came to a hermitage where they saw a cow yielding milk that tasted like nectar.
At home, their mother gave them water-mixed bread as 'milk', contrasting with the hermitage experience.
The narrator recalls a childhood experience where he tasted cow's milk and found it unsatisfying compared to other foods.
The narrator asks his mother for milk-based food.
The mother becomes worried and sad, embraces the narrator, and advises him that ascetics (Munis) should not drink milk and should instead rely on forest foods like bulbs, roots, and wild fruits.

attributes.advice_content: Ascetics should not seek worldly pleasures like milk

extraction_text: The mother explains that one cannot obtain milk, fine clothes, or worldly pleasures without pleasing Shiva (referred to as 'the deformed-eyed one', 'Sta-nu', and 'Shankara').

extraction_text: The mother instructs the narrator to devote himself entirely to Shiva (Shankara) to fulfill his wishes.

attributes.relationship: Upamanyu rejects Indra's potential favor, asserting his exclusive faith in Shiva.

attributes.relationship: Upamanyu positions Shiva as superior to all other deities, including those named.

extraction_text: King Mandhata, a powerful Chakravartin (universal monarch), was defeated and killed by the Trishula.

Parashurama killed the powerful Chakravartin king Kartavirya Arjuna in a fierce war.
Shiva wears the decorated battle-axe on his shoulder.
The narrator describes a vision of Shiva appearing with Brahma (the creator) on his left, seated on a chariot drawn by a swan.

attributes.description: They are described as having great souls and shining like three sacrificial fires.

extraction_text: The narrator observes the great god Shiva moving among and presiding over the gods.

extraction_text: The narrator begins to praise Shiva with hymns of adoration.

attributes.description: The praise enumerates Shiva's identities as: the supreme god over gods; Indra in form; wielder of the vajra, bow, sword, and trident; lord of dark phases; performer of white deeds; the Brahman among gods; the soul of all beings; the Purusha of Sankhya; the most successful yogi; the householder stage; the highest ruler; Kubera among Yakshas; Vishnu in sacrifices; Mount Meru among mountains; Vasishtha among sages; the moon among stars; the sun among luminaries; the lion among beasts; the bull among cattle; Vishnu among Adityas; Pavaka among Vasus; Garuda among birds; Ananta among serpents; the Sama Veda among Vedas; the 'Hundred Rudras' hymn; Sanatkumara among yogis; Kapila among Sankhya philosophers; Indra among Maruts; Yama among ancestors; the Brahmaloka among worlds; the path of liberation; the Ocean of Milk among seas; the Himalayas among mountains; the Brahmin among castes; the initiated twice-born among Brahmins; Time (Kala) the destroyer; and the embodiment of all supreme energies.

extraction_text: The narrator concludes the praise by saluting Shiva as the glorious god, the benevolent one to devotees, and the lord of yogis.

Upamanyu, with infinite devotion, offers water for washing feet and other hospitality items to Ishvara, presenting his loyalty with folded hands.

extraction_text: Ishvara, accompanied by his wife (Parvati), speaks joyfully to the thirty-three gods (Trayastrimsha) present, praising Upamanyu's unwavering, sacred, and focused devotion.

The narrator (Markandeya) prays to Sankara (Shiva) for eternal devotion, wisdom to know past/present/future, milk rice for himself and his relatives, and for Shiva's presence in his hermitage.
